correctness.rationale: A unique lowest-common-ancestor partition decomposes the Kendall objective. Singleton node costs sum to the exact caterpillar baseline. The exact variance of a random interleaving, Cauchy–Schwarz and five finite checks give g(a,b)≥ab/4 whenever both child sizes exceed one. A decreasing reciprocal-sum comparison proves the caterpillar baseline cross-term is at most ab/4−1/6, with equality only at the 2+2 split. Thus every nonsingleton split incurs at least 1/6; telescoping proves caterpillar-only equality and the exact runner-up core. Exact tests reproduce the pivotal five small cases, interleavings and every tree shape through fourteen leaves.

value.rationale: The February 2026 literature explicitly identifies the all-size caterpillar extremality question and the September 2026 paper supplies supporting observations only for finitely many cases. An all-size solution therefore closes a motivated problem, and the exact runner-up loss 1/6 with a complete shape characterization reveals a structural obstruction to diversity, useful for understanding nearby optimal domains. This is an invariant of a natural family, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
